subsystem: nonblocking welcome and diagnostic boot events
implementation: handwritten high-level C with named host phases; ROM execution belongs only to independent tests

implemented_routines.name: welcome banner and bounded key decision
implemented_routines.scope: 2381-count release/poll/scan/debounce phases, remembered raw pair, stable44 diagnostic branch, stable4/16 AC branch and native timeout asymmetry

implemented_routines.name: host control handshake
implemented_routines.scope: nonblocking flag2 begin/finish, flag4 notification, explicit inherited timer argument for5596

implemented_routines.name: diagnostic display and checksum
implemented_routines.scope: ROM version metadata, negative16-bit ROM sum, stored checksum predicate, raw port caption, externally supplied architectural read-test result, port setup and host polling

implemented_routines.name: diagnostic display patterns
implemented_routines.scope: white/black, border with native untouched row0, sixteen rows per alternating stripe value, complete LCD flush

implemented_routines.name: physical keyboard diagnostic
implemented_routines.scope: 49 two-digit counters and immutable ROM pair codes, single-bit encoding for all byte values, wrong-key redraw/retry

implemented_routines.name: diagnostic lifecycles
implemented_routines.scope: signature invalidation, cursor suppression, Alpha-only pattern waits, host diagnostic wait, delegated expanded contrast, physical-key test, final any-key prompt, contrast captured after wait and cold/default reset

host_contract: Every tick performs one bounded peripheral, raw-key or semantic-key phase and returns WAIT, READY, RESET or EXPORT.
Welcome may use a row-sensitive physical key callback; NULL reads the passive F040 port.
Ordinary diagnostic key waits use host8E01/8E02 packets. The host clears a delivered pair after the completed tick; the firmware does not clear those bytes.
READY from a boot WELCOME/DIAGNOSTIC request includes its ordinary D74C..D7AE mode tail. Standalone7044 ends after its default-screen return.
Host-owned strings, raw pairs, descriptor fields, cursor bitmaps and counters introduce no synthetic persistent CPU-local RAM writes.
prepared_policy: Native CPU stack8D00..8DED is excluded; every other RAM/MMIO byte and callback is compared.
The display-only adapter accepts the architectural7334 result at native7286. The standard host lifecycle supplies its verified A5 success result.
Complete 7044 tests use ordinary 80FB=0 with all annunciator/classifier workspaces compared; only CPU stack bytes are excluded.
Welcome stable-pair preparation at1E51C covers matrix rows unavailable from a single passive nativeF040 byte.
ROM checksum/version variants are deterministic test images changing metadata only; executable instructions and fonts remain original.
gaps: The native7334 CPU architecture/PSW test is not implemented or claimed as C instruction semantics.
Physical real-time interrupt, timer and keyboard scheduling remains with the host.
Existing raw-wait cursor-height bounds and key-controller event routing bounds remain explicit dependencies.
The ordinary main-event controller beyondD7AE remains separate.
